title: Check yourself: Scopes, the project file and environment expansion

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team commits `.mcp.json` with the header `Bearer ${NPM_TOKEN}` for a hosted package registry. Every developer exports the variable, yet the registry answers 401. What is the cause?

options.text: The file loads only after an interactive approval that the developers skipped
options.says: Ruled out because a server that waits for approval is not connected at all: "claude mcp list shows it as pending", and it does not answer with a 401.

options.text: Header values are expanded only for entries that start a local process
options.says: Ruled out because the documentation lists the places where expansion applies: `headers` ("for HTTP server authentication").

options.text: Claude Code reads names of this kind, which carry sign-in secrets, as empty
options.says: Credential names such as this one read as empty toward a remote endpoint.

options.text: A variable in a header needs a fallback after the colon and dash before use
options.says: Ruled out because a default is optional, and the plain form works: "expands to the value of environment variable".

questions.stem: A developer needs an integration that signs in with a personal account's token. It should exist in this repository only, and the token must never reach teammates through version control. Where should it be registered?

options.text: Local scope, the default for a newly added server
options.says: Local scope is the default and belongs to its owner and that one project. The guide names user-level scope for personal servers, and the product has a third scope between the two, which is the one that fits a single repository.

options.text: Project scope, kept in the shared `.mcp.json` file
options.says: Ruled out because "Selecting the wrong scope for a personal tool can leak credentials into a shared repo".

options.text: User scope, which loads the server in every project
options.says: Ruled out because user scope is for "services you frequently use across different projects", which is wider than this repository.

options.text: The local settings file, kept inside the repository
options.says: Ruled out because that file holds settings and not servers: "while the general local settings file is `.claude/settings.local.json` in the project".
